text:
Tara (CSM): Quick ask — can we assemble a lightweight customer-facing runbook for 'micro' onboarding customers (low-touch, limited budget) that focuses on cost-saving runtime patterns: caching, batching, streaming? Need something we can send during kickoff + include renewal-risk triggers.

Maria (CS Ops): +1. Short checklist + 1-pager is perfect. Include expected savings % and what we need from customer (usage pattern, latency SLO).

Eli (Solutions Eng): I can draft the tech section. Key suggestions: prefix caching, small batch windows, stream partial responses. Example configs below.

Sam (Runtime Eng): Also add warmup strategy to avoid cold-start token spikes — prefetch first N tokens after deploy and after scale events.

Tara (CSM): Ideal deliverables: 1) 1-page best-practices, 2) 4-step kickoff checklist, 3) renewal watchlist signals. Who takes what?

Maria (CS Ops): I'll own the 4-step kickoff checklist and renewal signals. Quick notes:
- Onboarding checklist: account preflight, telemetry access, sample traffic, go/no-go.
- Renewal watchlist (early warning): sustained >15% drop in cache hit rate, >20% token cost increase q/q, customer reports >2x tail latency spikes.

Eli (Solutions Eng): Tech 1-pager draft (short):
- Caching: prefer prefix/KV cache for deterministic prompts. Set TTLs = 24h for non-personalized prefills. Monitor cache_hit_rate.
- Batching: start with batch_window_ms = 50-100 for low-traffic customers. target batch size 4-8. Increase if latency budget allows.
- Streaming: flush every 32 tokens or 250ms to show early progress to user and reduce perceived latency.

Eli (Solutions Eng): Config snippet:
```
server: {
  prefetch: true,
  prefetch_tokens: 32,
  kv_cache_ttl_secs: 86400,
  batch_window_ms: 75,
  min_batch_size: 1,
  max_batch_size: 8,
  stream_flush_tokens: 32,
  stream_flush_ms: 250
}
```

Sam (Runtime Eng): Add operational items:
- Warmup hook: call /generate with a small sample to populate KV cache after deploy.
- Auto-fallback: route to smaller quantized model when latency SLOs fail.
- Metrics: cache_hit_rate, avg_p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_request, cost_per_1000_tokens.

Tara (CSM): Renewal signals template to include with the customer:
"We track cache hit rate, avg latency, and token spend. If we see persistent degradation in these we schedule a health call. Example trigger: cache_hit_rate < 60% for 7 days AND tokens_per_request increase > 15%"

Maria (CS Ops): Feedback capture snippet for enablement:
- Ask: "After first 2 weeks, did you see reduced cost/latency?" (Y/N)
- Follow-ups: free-text + ask for sample logs if issues.
- Slack template for CSM to collect: `@customer -- quick check: did you notice improvements after enablement?`

Tara (CSM): Can we standardize a short email to send post-kickoff with the 1-pager + action items?

Eli (Solutions Eng): Draft subject: "Redwood micro-onboard: cost & latency quick wins" body: 3 bullets + attach 1-pager.

Sam (Runtime Eng): Ops note: add a low-touch runbook step for us: if customer has >10% cost spike post-rollout, enable session tracing and collect sample requests for 48h.

Maria (CS Ops): I'll assemble everything into a single 1-pager and checklist by EOD Wednesday. Ping me for wording edits.

Tara (CSM): Awesome. I'll prep a renewal-watch alert in our tracking doc and add the customer-facing email template.

cs-bot: Reminder: shared doc created — https://redwood.app/docs/micro-onboard-runbook (created by Maria)

Tara (CSM): TY team. We'll trial this on 2 low-touch accounts next week and capture outcomes.

Sam (Runtime Eng): +1 :rocket:

Eli (Solutions Eng): Happy to review the 1-pager and tweak the configs.

Maria (CS Ops): Will post draft link here when ready: will be in the doc above.
